evals.prompt: every time i ask claude to write release notes for our app it formats them differently. sometimes bullet lists, sometimes paragraphs. can you set something up so it always does: Summary section, then Breaking Changes, then Fixes, pulling from git log since the last tag?
evals.expected_output: A skill folder with a trigger-rich description, a body encoding the fixed three-section format with a verbatim example, and a git-log step (likely scripted).
assertions: A SKILL.md is created with valid frontmatter (name and description)
The description states when to trigger, in third person, with concrete trigger phrases
The body specifies the exact section order: Summary, Breaking Changes, Fixes
The body or a script covers pulling commits since the last git tag
At least one concrete input-to-output example is included

evals.prompt:
I wrote this skill for generating our weekly metrics report but claude never seems to use it unless I literally type the skill name. here's the SKILL.md:

---
name: metrics-report
description: Generates the weekly metrics report.
---

# Metrics Report

You MUST ALWAYS query the analytics DB first. You should then handle the data appropriately and process it as needed into a report. NEVER use the staging DB.

can you fix it?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that the one-line description under-triggers, a rewritten pushy third-person description with trigger phrases and negative triggers, and a body rewrite replacing MUST/ALWAYS/handle/appropriately with rule-plus-reason instructions.
assertions: The response identifies the thin description as the triggering root cause
The rewritten description includes concrete trigger phrases and when-to-use language
ALL-CAPS directives (MUST, ALWAYS, NEVER) are removed or reframed with reasons
Vague verbs (handle, process, appropriately, as needed) are replaced with specific actions
The staging-DB rule survives, restated with its reason

evals.prompt: we keep pasting the same instructions into chat for cleaning vendor CSVs before import (drop rows with empty SKU, normalize date columns to ISO, fail if more than 5% of rows get dropped). make this a proper reusable thing for the team. it should be deterministic - same file in, same file out.
evals.expected_output: A skill whose deterministic cleaning steps live in a bundled script (not prose), with the body invoking the script, and a description matching casual phrasings like 'clean this vendor csv'.
assertions: The deterministic cleaning logic is delivered as a bundled script, not as prose instructions
The script is non-interactive and reports errors with specifics (e.g., which rows dropped, the drop percentage)
The 5% drop threshold appears in the script or body with its failure behavior
The SKILL.md body instructs running the script rather than re-deriving the logic
The description covers casual trigger phrasings for CSV cleaning
